source.title: Is the Skip Connection Provable to Reform the Neural Network Loss Landscape?
source.authors: Lifu Wang; Bo Shen; Ningrui Zhao; Zhi-Yuan Zhang

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. A proof passage in Theorem 11 appears to contain a typographical inconsistency in its variable names; the theorem statement and discussion are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper theoretically analyzes whether skip connections improve the loss landscape of deep ReLU networks, using sub-level-set connectivity and local-minimum depth rather than training-error measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a theorem about local-minimum depth and a loss-surface visualization. It does not report benchmark training-error results or compare training outcomes across network depths. Cited results from other work are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study proves loss-landscape connectivity and escape-barrier bounds, rather than measuring training error, gradient-descent outcomes, or training speed. Neither its theorem nor its qualitative loss-surface visualization tests any stated version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors conclude that their skip-connected architecture has shallow strict local minima above a corresponding sparse two-layer ReLU benchmark, with escape-barrier bound O(m^((η−1)/n)) shrinking as width grows under their assumptions. They interpret this as a theoretical explanation for skip connections' effectiveness; they do not establish gradient-based training performance.
record.recipe_differences: The paper gives a theoretical loss-landscape analysis of a specified skip-connected ReLU architecture; it does not test the benchmark training recipes in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The theorem depends on convex loss, bounded inputs and outputs, regularization, a ReLU skip-connected architecture, and the stated width and approximation conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 11 constructs paths whose regularized loss stays below max(Fw*, λ) + O(m^((η−1)/n)) for the specified skip-connected ReLU architecture.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the stated boundedness, loss, regularization, and width assumptions, strict local minima above the sparse two-layer ReLU benchmark have escape barriers bounded by O(m^((η−1)/n)).

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 1 is described as showing a smoother, better projected loss surface for ResNet-56 with skip connections; no training-error comparison across depths is reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Skip connections improve the qualitative appearance of the plotted ResNet-56 loss surface.

record.peer_reviewed: International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence
record.problems: The evidence is theoretical and conditional on the stated assumptions; it provides no empirical optimization or benchmark training-error results. The loss-surface visualization is not accompanied by quantitative measurements in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying results. Figure 1 is described as showing a smoother and better ResNet-56 loss surface with skip connections, but the supplied text gives no numeric measurement and does not connect that visualization to training error; it is not extracted as a result row for V3.

record.verdict_notes: The original-source findings cited in the introduction and related work are not this study's results. Figure 1 is already declared in rows_left_out. The initialization remark supplies no comparison bearing on V4.

rows.subject: deep ReLU neural network with a skip connection (f1)
rows.size_stated: m is the dimension of W1 ∈ Rm×n; l < mη, η < 1
rows.operation_detail: Theorem bounds the depth of paths connecting parameter points through the loss landscape.

conditions.value: convex L satisfying assumptions 1 and 2, with the stated regularization
two-layer ReLU network with l-term approximation

rows.measure: For any ξA, ξB with F(ξ{A,B}) ≤ λ, a path exists with F(γ(t)) ≤ max(Fw*, λ) + O(m^(η−1)/n).
rows.note: The result is a theoretical bound on loss-landscape paths for a specified skip-connected model. It does not measure training error or show that gradient-based training attains the bound.
rows.check: Theorem 11 bounds loss barriers along existing continuous parameter paths; it does not show that training follows those paths or that identity shortcuts prevent training-error degradation. The bound is O(m^((η−1)/n)), not O(m^(η−1)/n); n belongs inside the exponent. This is a theoretical result, not a measurement of a claim version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
